description:
## Problem
With the tuned date-first sort key at SF1, three queries run slower than `notuning`, and rows read does not explain it:

| Query | Time | Rows read |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 | 1.43× | 0.54× |
| Q5 | 1.49× | 0.84× |
| Q18 | 1.77× | 2.15× |

The ADR blamed lost order-key ordering in `lineitem` (join locality), but that was never tested.

## Change
- Use the harness to compare untuned and sort-only. For each slow query, record peak memory, the join algorithm ClickHouse chose, rows and bytes read, `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` and `EXPLAIN PIPELINE`, and `system.query_log` ProfileEvents.
- Add two layout arms: `(L_ORDERKEY, L_SHIPDATE)` and `(L_SHIPDATE, L_ORDERKEY)`. The expectation is that an order-key-first key loses the date pruning that made Q6, Q14 and Q15 faster. Measure that rather than assume it.
- State the cause with evidence, or state "unproven" and list what was ruled out.

## Decision gate
- Any template change goes through the benefit rule (`tuning-evidence-benefit-rule-20261008`). This item produces findings only.

## Guardrails (must preserve)
- Report every query in each arm, not only the three slow ones.
- No template edits in this item.

## Process guardrails
- One PR per item against `develop`, via the AGENTS.md worktree flow (`make worktree-claim BRANCH=...`, `make agent-write-preflight`).
- Stage explicit paths; never `git add -A`.
- Re-read every file:line anchor before editing. Anchors are from develop 5ca12e6ca.
